name: Croatia: Istria, Zagreb, Plitvice, Kvarner and the islands

destination.name: Croatia: Istria, Zagreb, Plitvice, Kvarner and the islands
destination.pitch: The country is not the Dalmatian coast: it is a Central European capital, an Istrian peninsula that cooks and pours better than the rest of it, a karst interior of lakes and ridges, and then the islands.

because.nature: Travertine lakes at Plitvice and Krka, 160m cliffs on Dugi otok, the Velebit ridge above the coast, and eighty-nine waterless islands in one national park.
because.exploration: Four inheritances in one country: Roman Pula, Venetian island towns, Habsburg Zagreb and Opatija, and a Yugoslav military island closed to foreigners until 1989.
because.food: Istria is the real food region: white truffle from September, olive oils that win international panels, malvazija, and oysters and lamb further south. Book the good kitchens.
because.relaxation: You swim off rock and concrete rather than sand, in water that stays usable into October, and the smaller islands empty out completely by the second week of September.
because.culture: A cathedral built entirely of interlocking stone, Meštrović's own villa, Rijeka's modern art in a sugar refinery, and a hill town given to artists in the 1960s.
because.adventure: Anića kuk in Paklenica is the biggest climbing wall in this corner of Europe, the Premužić trail runs the Velebit ridge, and sea kayaking off the islands is genuinely good.
because.city: Zagreb is a proper Central European city with markets, museums and a Saturday coffee ritual, and it is nobody's beach holiday. Two or three nights, no more.

destination.caveat: Distances are longer than the map implies once ferries are involved, and the coast runs on a July and August schedule that doubles prices: Dubrovnik is a cruise port by 10:00, its walls cost about 35 euro, and half the island konobas and boats shut from October to Easter. Put together for you just n Put together for you just now from what I know, rather than checked against today's opening times. Worth confirming anything you're pinning the trip on.

cities.name: Zagreb
cities.base: The Lower Town between Ban Jelačić square and Zrinjevac, or below the Upper Town on Tkalčićeva if noise does not bother you. Everything except the contemporary art museum is a twenty-minute walk.

cities.name: Zagorje: Trakošćan, Kumrovec and Veliki Tabor
cities.base: Nobody needs a bed up here. It is 90 minutes north of Zagreb and a full day by car, and the castles and Tito's village are within 45 minutes of each other on small green roads.

cities.name: Varaždin
cities.base: A day trip, not a base. Seventy-five minutes from Zagreb by car or train, and the baroque centre, the castle and the topiary cemetery are all inside twenty minutes on foot.

cities.name: Plitvice Lakes
cities.base: Mukinje or Jezerce, the park workers' villages ten minutes below Entrance 2, or a farmhouse at Rastovača. The only reason to sleep here is being at a gate at 07:00 before the coaches.

cities.name: Rastoke and Slunj
cities.base: No beds needed. Thirty-five minutes north of Plitvice on the road to Zagreb, so it is the stop you make on the way out rather than a day of its own.

cities.name: Rovinj
cities.base: Inside the old town if you can carry a bag up the steps, otherwise the streets just behind the market. Cars stay off the peninsula and the town is ten minutes end to end.

cities.name: Pula
cities.base: Between the Forum and the market hall, west of the amphitheatre. The old town is small and flat; the swimming is 20 minutes south at Verudela or an hour at Kamenjak.

cities.name: Brijuni islands
cities.base: There is one hotel on Veli Brijun and no reason to use it. You go from Fažana on a booked boat, spend four hours, and come back; the island is a national park and movement on it is guided.

cities.name: Motovun and the Mirna valley
cities.base: Up in the walled town for the valley at dawn, or down at Livade for the truffle restaurants. You need a car either way, and the last stretch into Motovun is walked or shuttled.

cities.name: Opatija and Rijeka
cities.base: Opatija for the promenade, Volosko for the food and quiet, Lovran for cheaper rooms. Rijeka is 25 minutes by bus and is a working port city rather than somewhere to sleep.

cities.name: Učka and Vela Draga
cities.base: A mountain, not a town: a pass road, a summit tower and a canyon viewpoint. You sleep in Opatija or Lovran and drive up to Poklon at 922m in 45 minutes.

cities.name: Krk island
cities.base: You can sleep on Krk, but from Opatija or Rab it is a better day than a base. The bridge means no ferry queue, and Vrbnik and Baška are an hour apart on decent road.

cities.name: Rab
cities.base: Inside the old town on the spit, or Banjol and Palit for cheaper rooms and parking. You arrive on the Stinica to Mišnjak ferry, fifteen minutes and frequent; Lopar and Kalifront need a car.

cities.name: Cres
cities.base: Reached by the Valbiska to Merag ferry from Krk, or Brestova to Porozina. From Rab there is a seasonal Lopar boat. A day if you take the first crossing; adding Lošinj needs a night.

cities.name: Zadar
cities.base: On the peninsula inside the walls if you accept the summer noise, or Voštarnica across the bridge for quiet and parking. The old town is fifteen minutes end to end and the boats leave from it.

cities.name: Pag island
cities.base: Sleep in Zadar and drive up: the bridge is an hour north, Novalja another 45 minutes. Nothing on Pag needs a night unless you came for the clubs at Zrće.

cities.name: Paklenica and the Velebit
cities.base: Starigrad-Paklenica has rooms but no reason to use them for one gorge. It is an hour north of Zadar, the park gate opens early, and the walls above the canyon are the biggest in this half of Europe.

cities.name: The Kornati and Telašćica
cities.base: Eighty-nine islands with no fresh water and almost nobody living on them, so you sleep in Zadar, Murter or Sali and go out for the day by boat. The park fee is usually inside the ticket.

cities.name: Šibenik
cities.base: The lanes between the cathedral and the Barone fortress, on the steps. It is a stair town, so ask whether the room has parking below it; the Krka boats and the buses are both on the front.

cities.name: Split
cities.base: Varoš or Manuš, just outside the palace walls rather than inside them. Two nights is plenty on a country trip: the Dalmatian coast has a plan of its own and this one is the rest of Croatia.

cities.name: Brač
cities.base: Bol for Zlatni rat and the Vidova gora path, Supetar if you are coming and going by ferry from Split. The island is big and the bus is thin, so a car pays for itself in a day.

cities.name: Vis
cities.base: Kut, the eastern half of Vis town, or Komiža for the Blue Cave boats and the sunsets. The car ferry from Split is 2h20 and the catamaran 1h25; a scooter is enough for the island.

cities.name: Biševo and the Blue Cave
cities.base: Fifteen people live here and there are no rooms worth the crossing. Boats go from Komiža in 30 minutes and from Vis town in an hour, and the cave wants late morning light.

cities.name: Korčula
cities.base: The old town if you want to walk out into it, Lumbarda for sand and wine, Pupnat for a farmhouse. Arrive by catamaran from Split or the Orebić car ferry; the old town itself is car-free.

cities.name: Mljet
cities.base: Pomena and Polače have small hotels, and a night there is pleasant and unnecessary. From Korčula or Dubrovnik it is a boat, a bicycle and a park ticket, then the boat back.

cities.name: Pelješac: Dingač, Postup and Ston
cities.base: Orebić and Trpanj have beds, but the peninsula is a driving day from Korčula or on the way to Dubrovnik. Ferry Domince to Orebić in 15 minutes, then one road the length of it.

cities.name: Dubrovnik
cities.base: Ploce or Lapad, outside the walls, or Gruž by the port if you are taking ferries. Rooms inside the old town cost double, the street noise carries off stone, and every arrival involves steps.

cities.name: The Elaphiti: Lopud, Šipan and Koločep
cities.base: Lopud has a few hotels and no cars. Most people go for the day on the Jadrolinija boat from Gruž, which is 50 minutes to Lopud and 90 to Šipan and runs to a timetable you must check first.

cities.name: Osijek and Slavonia
cities.base: Tvrđa or the boulevard between it and the centre. The city is flat, the trams work, and you want a car for Kopački rit and Vukovar. It is a detour most Croatia trips skip.

cities.name: Kopački rit and Vukovar
cities.base: Thirty minutes northeast of Osijek and no beds you would choose. The floodplain is a morning by boat, and Vukovar is an hour the other way and a much heavier afternoon.

outings.name: Zagreb on foot: Dolac, the Upper Town and Tkalčićeva
outings.why: Market at 08:00, the Upper Town museums, the cannon at noon, then Lower Town cafes and Tkalčićeva after dark. Flat and entirely walkable, and most museums shut on Mondays.
outings.season: All year. Advent market late November to early January.
outings.fallback: Mimara and the contemporary art museum across the Sava if it rains.

outings.name: Zagorje castles: Trakošćan and Kumrovec
outings.why: Ninety minutes north into green hills for a furnished lake castle, then Tito's birth village kept as an open-air museum of Zagorje cottages. Veliki Tabor fits if you drive well.
outings.season: All year. Best in spring; castles busy with school groups.
outings.fallback: Varaždin instead: the baroque centre, the old castle and the topiary cemetery.

outings.name: Plitvice Lakes: Upper and Lower
outings.why: Sixteen terraced lakes and the boardwalks between them, done as the long loop from Entrance 2. About 18km of nearly flat walking plus a boat and a shuttle. The boat is the bottleneck.
outings.season: All year; about 40 euro in summer, 10 in winter.
outings.fallback: Lower lakes and Veliki slap only, three hours from Entrance 1, then Rastoke on the way out.

outings.name: The truffle day: Livade, Hum and Grožnjan
outings.why: A morning hunt in the Motovun forest, lunch at Livade, then the hill towns on the north side of the Mirna. White truffle is September to January; anything else is black or frozen stock.
outings.season: All year. White truffle September to January.
outings.fallback: Grožnjan, Oprtalj and a long lunch at Zigante, with no dogs involved.

outings.name: Brijuni: Veli Brijun
outings.why: A booked boat from Fažana and then a tourist train round Tito's island: Roman villa, safari park, and a photo museum of the Non-Aligned Movement. You cannot wander off the route alone.
outings.season: All year; full programme May to October.
outings.fallback: Fažana, the Vodnjan mummies and the Peroj olive road instead.

outings.name: Učka: Vojak from Poklon
outings.why: From the Poklon pass at 922m to the stone tower on Vojak at 1,401m, ninety minutes each way through beech. Istria on one side, the Kvarner islands on the other, cloud on top often.
outings.season: April to November. Ice and snow on top in winter.
outings.fallback: Vela Draga canyon viewpoint, then lunch at Lovranska Draga, about two hours.

outings.name: Krk: Vrbnik and Baška
outings.why: Over the bridge to a cliff town that makes žlahtina, then south to the long pebble beach at Baška under bare hills. Easy driving, no ferry, and the bora can close the bridge for a day.
outings.season: All year; swimming June to early October.
outings.fallback: Krk town, the cathedral and the Frankopan castle, about three hours.

outings.name: Cres: Lubenice and the Beli vultures
outings.why: A ferry and a slow island road to a cliff village of a dozen people, then the griffon colony above Beli. Two hours of driving on the day, and the beach under Lubenice is a hard climb back.
outings.season: May to October. Lubenice concerts July and August.
outings.fallback: Valun, its Glagolitic tablet and the Cres town harbour, about four hours.

outings.name: Northern Velebit: the Premužić trail from Zavižan
outings.why: The 1930s dry-stone path along the ridge from Zavižan, walked as far as the Rossijevo shelter and back. The emptiest big landscape in Croatia, and the access road up is long and rough.
outings.season: Late June to October; Zavižan road closed by snow.
outings.fallback: Zavižan botanical garden and the weather station, then back down to the coast road.

outings.name: Velebit: Paklenica and Anića kuk
outings.why: Into the Velika Paklenica gorge under a 350m wall, up to the Lugarnica hut and back, with the Manita peć cave as an option. Shaded and stony, and it cooks after 11:00 in summer.
outings.season: April to June and September to October are best.
outings.fallback: The gorge mouth, the bunker tunnel and Manita peć cave, about three hours.

outings.name: The Kornati by boat from Murter or Sali
outings.why: Eighty-nine islands of bare rock, a park fee, two swimming stops and lunch on board, usually with Telašćica and Lake Mir included. Nothing on the day is shaded and wind cancels it.
outings.season: April to October. Cancelled in strong wind.
outings.fallback: Telašćica on the Zadar car ferry to Brbinj, or the Ugljan ferry for a half day.

outings.name: Krka and Skradin
outings.why: Skradinski buk, the travertine staircase, plus the boat up to Visovac monastery. Swimming at the falls has been banned since 2021, which removed the main reason people used to come.
outings.season: All year; boats and full price June to September.
outings.fallback: Skradin and the Krka boat to Visovac only, then a long lunch in Skradin.

outings.name: Vidova gora and Zlatni rat
outings.why: Two hours up from Bol to 778m, the highest point on any Adriatic island, with the spit directly below, then down to swim off it. No water and no shade on the climb.
outings.season: April to October. Too hot after 10:00 midsummer.
outings.fallback: Drive up to Vidova gora from Nerežišća, then Blaca hermitage by boat from Bol.

outings.name: Vis: the military tunnels and Stiniva
outings.why: A jeep tour of Tito's cave, a submarine pen and a rocket base on an island closed to foreigners until 1989, then the walk down into Stiniva cove. The tracks need a guide and a 4x4.
outings.season: April to October. Guides thin out in winter.
outings.fallback: Mount Hum and the Komiža fishermen's museum, about four hours.

outings.name: Biševo and the Blue Cave
outings.why: A boat to Biševo, then a rowing boat through a 1.5m gap into a cave lit from beneath. It needs late morning sun and a flat sea, and it is twenty minutes inside for a half-day trip.
outings.season: May to September. Any swell shuts the cave.
outings.fallback: Stiniva, Srebrna and the south coast caves by boat, or the island military tour.

outings.name: Mljet: the saltwater lakes
outings.why: A catamaran or excursion boat to the west end, then 9km of flat lakeside path by bicycle and the park launch to the monastery islet. Most of the day is the timetable, not the island.
outings.season: April to October. Park boats barely run in winter.
outings.fallback: Polače and Veliko jezero on foot for three hours if you only get a late boat.

outings.name: A Pelješac wine day: Dingač and Postup
outings.why: The ferry to Orebić, cellars at Potomje, and the one-lane tunnel through the ridge to the Dingač slope above the sea. Plavac mali off 45-degree limestone, and somebody has to not drink.
outings.season: All year. Harvest and best cellar visits in September.
outings.fallback: Two cellars in Potomje and lunch at Trstenik, with half the driving.

outings.name: Dubrovnik: the walls at 08:00 and Srđ at dusk
outings.why: The walls before the cruise passengers land, then the Rector's Palace and War Photo in the heat, and up Srđ for the siege museum at dusk. The walls alone are about 35 euro.
outings.season: All year; walls close early in winter and in storms.
outings.fallback: War Photo Limited, the Franciscan cloister and Lokrum if the walls are a queue.

outings.name: The Elaphiti: Lopud and Šipan
outings.why: The Jadrolinija boat from Gruž to car-free islands: a Franciscan fortress, nobles' villas and the only real sand near Dubrovnik at Šunj. Check the timetable before anything else.
outings.season: All year; more sailings June to September.
outings.fallback: Lokrum on the fifteen-minute boat, four hours, with the salt lake to swim in.

outings.name: Kopački rit by punt
outings.why: The Drava and Danube floodplain from a flat boat, with white-tailed eagles and black storks. Spring flood and autumn migration are the point; July is mosquitoes and low water.
outings.season: March to June and September to November.
outings.fallback: The Vukovar water tower and the Danube bank: a harder and more necessary day.

places.name: Dolac market
places.note: The red-umbrella produce deck above a covered fish and dairy hall, two minutes off the main square. Go before 10:00; by early afternoon stalls are packing up, and Sunday is a short morning only.

places.name: Zagreb Cathedral
places.note: The 2020 earthquake took the top off the south spire and the interior has been shut or only partly open ever since, with scaffolding on the facade. Check the state of it before you plan a morning around it.

places.name: St Mark's Church
places.note: The 1880 tiled roof with the coats of arms of Croatia, Dalmatia, Slavonia and the city is the whole point. The interior is usually locked outside Mass, so this is a five-minute stop and the square around it is better.

places.name: Lotrscak Tower and the Grič cannon
places.note: A 13th-century tower on the old wall, climbable up wooden stairs for the best view over the Lower Town roofs. The cannon on the top floor is fired every day at noon and it is much louder than you expect.

places.name: The Zagreb funicular
places.note: Sixty-six metres of track and 55 seconds, which makes it one of the shortest public funiculars anywhere, running since 1890. It is a novelty; the stairs beside it are free and barely slower.

places.name: Museum of Broken Relationships
places.note: Objects donated by strangers with the story of the breakup attached, from an axe to a wedding dress. It sounds like a gimmick and is the most affecting hour in the city; it stays open late.

places.name: Croatian Museum of Naïve Art
places.note: One floor of the Hlebine school painters who worked on glass in a Podravina village, Generalić above all. Forty-five minutes, weekend hours are much shorter than weekday ones.

places.name: Mimara Museum
places.note: Ante Topić Mimara's collection given to the state in 1972: Egyptian and Chinese rooms, then a picture gallery whose bigger attributions are argued about. Closed Mondays and half empty on any day.

places.name: Museum of Contemporary Art
places.note: Across the Sava in Novi Zagreb, with the Gorgona group, Sanja Iveković and Carsten Höller's slide running down the outside of the building. Closed Mondays, and a tram ride rather than a walk.

places.name: Strossmartre promenade
places.note: The tree-lined walk along the old Upper Town wall with the whole Lower Town under it. In summer it fills with bands, bars and second-hand book stalls in the evenings and nothing much happens by day.

places.name: Mirogoj cemetery
places.note: Hermann Bollé's arcaded cemetery of 1876: a long brick colonnade of cupolas and ivy, with Catholic, Orthodox, Jewish and Muslim graves in the same ground. A 106 bus or a twenty-minute walk uphill from Kaptol.

places.name: Maksimir park
places.note: An English-style park laid out from 1794 with lakes, an oak wood and the zoo, ten minutes out on the 11 or 12 tram. This is the local Sunday and the only real shade on an August afternoon.

places.name: Grič tunnel
places.note: A Second World War air-raid tunnel under the Upper Town, reopened in 2016 as a through-route with occasional exhibitions. Two minutes end to end, twelve degrees inside, and genuinely useful in a heatwave.

places.name: Saturday špica on Cvjetni trg
places.note: Saturday late morning is a civic ritual here: the city sits outside on Bogovićeva and Preradovićeva from about 11:00 to 14:00, dressed for it, over one coffee. Any other day it is just a cafe.

places.name: Tkalčićeva street
places.note: One long line of terraces up a filled-in stream bed, and where everyone ends up after dark. The coffee is better a street either side and the beer costs a euro more for the position.

places.name: Vinodol
places.note: A courtyard grill under a vine doing veal and lamb from under the peka bell, which you order a few hours ahead. The most reliable old-school Zagreb table in the centre and not expensive for what it is.

places.name: Lari & Penati
places.note: A six-table kitchen on Petrinjska with a blackboard that changes every day and no pretence about it. Weekday lunch only, so put it on a working day or you will find the shutter down.

places.name: Trakošćan castle
places.note: A 13th-century fort rebuilt in the 1850s as a romantic fantasy, fully furnished, with a lake walk around it. The most visited castle in the country, and it is full of school groups from 10:00.

places.name: Kumrovec and Tito's birthplace
places.note: The village where Josip Broz was born in 1892, kept as an open-air museum of Zagorje cottages with his house at the centre. The politics are handled carefully; the ethnographic half is genuinely good.

places.name: Veliki Tabor
places.note: A five-towered late-Gothic fortress on a vineyard hill, restored and far emptier than Trakošćan. The farm restaurant below it does the štrukli that are the other reason to drive up here.

places.name: Stari grad castle
places.note: A white Renaissance fortress with a moat and a wooden drawbridge, holding the city museum's period rooms. The grass bastions around it are the town's park and free to walk.

places.name: The baroque centre and the Korzo
places.note: Croatia's capital until a fire in 1776 sent the administration to Zagreb, which is why the centre is a set of untouched pastel palaces. An hour on foot, most of it pedestrianised.

places.name: Varaždin municipal cemetery
places.note: From 1905 Hermann Haller spent forty years clipping this into walls and corridors of cypress and box, so it reads as architecture rather than a graveyard. Twenty minutes and unlike anything else here.

places.name: The Lower Lakes and Veliki slap
places.note: The 78m waterfall and the boardwalks under the travertine barriers, on the half everyone does. In summer the ticket is about 40 euro with a timed entry, and by 10:00 the boardwalk is single file.

places.name: The Upper Lakes
places.note: Twelve lakes stepping up through beech forest above Kozjak, with better colour and a third of the people. Covered by the same ticket; the boardwalks here are the first to close in ice.

places.name: The P1 boat across Kozjak
places.note: An electric launch across the largest lake, the link between the two halves of the park and included in the ticket. It is also the bottleneck: thirty-minute queues in the middle of an August day.

places.name: The lakes frozen
places.note: From November to March the ticket drops to about 10 euro, the boats stop and the upper boardwalks are roped off or icy. What you get instead is frozen travertine and almost nobody on it.

places.name: Lička kuća
places.note: A big stone-and-timber room at Entrance 1 doing Lika lamb, spit-roasted, with trout and cheese strudel. It is a coach stop and it is still the best cooked food within fifteen kilometres.

places.name: Mukinje and Jezerce
places.note: The two park-workers' villages where most of the honest rooms are, ten minutes below Entrance 2 on a forest path. Not a sight; useful to know you can walk to the gate rather than drive.

places.name: Barać caves
places.note: A guided limestone cave twenty minutes northwest of the park, dry, cool and well run. The real alternative when Plitvice is sold out or the boardwalks are shut in rain.

places.name: Rastoke mill village
places.note: A hamlet built on travertine steps where the Slunjčica drops into the Korana, with mill wheels still turning under the houses. Twenty minutes' worth of village, better in low light, and a small entry fee.

places.name: Pod Rastockim krovom
places.note: Trout and cheese pie on a terrace directly over the falls, family-run for decades. The obvious lunch on the drive between Plitvice and Zagreb.

places.name: St Euphemia's church and campanile
places.note: A 60m Venetian bell tower copied from San Marco with the saint as a weathervane on top. The climb is a wooden ladder-stair that is not for everyone, and the tower shuts outside the season.

places.name: Grisia and the old town lanes
places.note: One steep street of limestone polished to glass, hung with paintings for one Sunday in August. Walk it at 07:00 or after 20:00; between those it is the day-trip coaches from Pula and Trieste.

places.name: Zlatni rt forest park
places.note: Baron Hütterott's 1890 planting of cedar, cypress and pine on the headland south of town, with rock swimming and a climbing wall at the end. Pines to the water's edge and no sand anywhere.

places.name: Batana House
places.note: One room on the flat-bottomed boat this town fished from, and the bitinada singing that went with it. Small and specific, and in summer it runs a supper in a waterside spacio with the songs live.

places.name: Rovinj morning market
places.note: Figs, olive oil, cheese and truffles in season, with a small fish hall on the corner. Half of it is souvenir stalls now; the produce end is still worth the early walk.

places.name: Sveta Katarina and Crveni otok
places.note: Taxi-boats run all day from the harbour to two wooded islets with rock swimming and one bar each. Crveni otok has the better water, Katarina the quicker return, and the last boats back are early.

places.name: The Lim channel
places.note: A 10km drowned karst valley of oyster and mussel rafts northeast of town, reached by boat trip or by road to the shellfish shacks at its head. The boat trips also sell a fake pirate cave; skip that part.

places.name: Monte
places.note: Croatia's first Michelin star, up against the church walls, with tasting menus around 110 euro. Book weeks ahead and do not turn up in winter, because it closes for several months.

places.name: Kantinon
places.note: A high-ceilinged former wine cellar on the harbour doing whole fish, pasta with shellfish and malvazija from the barrel. Roughly half what the terraces fifty metres away charge.

places.name: Valentino
places.note: Cushions on the rocks at sea level with your drink in your hand and the sun going down behind the islands. Overpriced by design, and the position is genuinely unbeatable in this town.

places.name: The Amphitheatre
places.note: A first-century arena that still has its full outer ring on the sea side because the stone was never carted away. Go at opening or after 19:00; in July it doubles as a concert venue and shuts early.

places.name: The Forum and the Temple of Augustus
places.note: The Roman forum is still the town square, and the temple on it was rebuilt after an Allied bomb hit it in 1944. Twenty minutes inside, and the cafes on the square are fairly priced.

places.name: The Arch of the Sergii and Kandlerova
places.note: A 27 BC triumphal arch at the end of the old shopping street, with a James Joyce statue outside a cafe near it from his unhappy year teaching here in 1904. Fifteen minutes plus whatever the coffee takes.

places.name: Zerostrasse tunnels
places.note: Austro-Hungarian shelter tunnels under the fortress hill, cool and half-lit, with a small exhibition inside. Ten minutes of relief when the arena has cooked you.

places.name: Lighting Giants at Uljanik
places.note: Dean Skira lit the shipyard's eight cranes in 2014 and they run a colour programme after dark in summer. The yard itself has been in and out of bankruptcy, which makes it a stranger thing to watch.

places.name: Cape Kamenjak
places.note: Thirty kilometres of unfenced limestone coast at the tip of the peninsula, with dinosaur footprints, a cliff jump and the Safari Bar in the scrub. Entry is per car, the tracks are white gravel, and there is no shade.

places.name: Pula market hall
places.note: An 1886 cast-iron and glass hall with fish on the ground floor and cheese, oil and pršut upstairs. The first-floor grill counters do the cheapest good lunch in the city.

places.name: Milan 1967
places.note: An old-fashioned family fish restaurant with a serious Istrian wine list of several hundred bottles. It looks like a hotel dining room and cooks better than anything on the seafront.

places.name: Cvajner
places.note: A former bank on the Forum turned cafe and gallery, with fresco fragments on bare walls and mismatched furniture. The best coffee stop in Pula and it stays open late.

places.name: Veli Brijun and the safari park
places.note: Tito's state island: holm oak and mown lawn, a Roman villa, and a safari park of animals descended from gifts by Nehru and Indira Gandhi. Access is the booked Fažana boat and movement on the island is guided.

places.name: Tito on Brijuni photo museum
places.note: Two rooms of photographs of Tito with Burton, Loren and half the Non-Aligned Movement, plus a taxidermy hall. The strangest political archive in the country and included in the island ticket.

places.name: The dinosaur footprints at Ploce
places.note: Theropod prints pressed into the limestone at the island's southern tip, reached on the tourist train loop or a rented bicycle. Faint in flat light and clear when the sun is low.

places.name: The Motovun wall circuit
places.note: A complete Venetian wall walk around a hill town of 500 people, with the Mirna valley 270m below and morning fog in it in autumn. The car park is at two thirds height; the rest is on foot or a shuttle.

places.name: Livade and Zigante
places.note: The village where Giancarlo Zigante dug up a 1.31kg white truffle in 1999, now a restaurant and a shop. White truffle is September to January; outside that you are eating the black one or frozen stock.

places.name: A truffle hunt with dogs
places.note: Two hours in the oak forest behind a lagotto, then an omelette with whatever was found. The autumn white-truffle version is the real thing; the summer hunts turn up black truffles you would not pay for.

places.name: Grožnjan
places.note: An all-but-abandoned hill town handed to artists and a summer music school in the 1960s, so every second doorway is a studio. Busy with students in July, dead quiet from November, and 25 minutes each way.

places.name: Hum and the Glagolitic Alley
places.note: Twenty-odd residents, two streets and a claim to be the smallest town in the world, with a road in lined with monuments to the Glagolitic script. The konoba pours biska, the local mistletoe brandy.

places.name: Kotli and the Mirna pools
places.note: An abandoned mill hamlet below Hum with rock pools worn into the riverbed. Swimmable in June, often a trickle by late August, and the path down from the car is short and slippery.

places.name: Kabola winery
places.note: Malvazija aged in amphorae buried in the ground, tasted on a terrace over the Momjan valley. Book ahead: it is a working farm, not a tasting room with staff waiting.

places.name: Konoba Toklarija
places.note: An 800-year-old olive mill where one cook serves one long menu to about a dozen people. You book days ahead, you eat what arrives, and it takes the whole evening.

places.name: Motovun Film Festival
places.note: Five nights in late July when the main square becomes a screen and the town's population multiplies by twenty. Excellent if you came for it; if you did not, avoid those dates entirely.

places.name: The Lungomare
places.note: Twelve kilometres of seafront path from Volosko through Opatija to Lovran, built for Habsburg convalescents from 1889. Flat, lit, and the one stretch of this coast you can do without a car.

places.name: Villa Angiolina and its park
places.note: The 1844 villa that turned a fishing village into a Habsburg resort, with a park of camellias, sequoias and the Japanese banana that became the town's symbol. Closed Mondays.

places.name: Volosko harbour
places.note: The fishing village at the north end of the Lungomare, all steps, boats and no promenade hotels. Two of the best kitchens on this coast are in it, which is the main reason to walk up.

places.name: Swimming off the concrete
places.note: There is almost no sand on this coast: you swim off concrete platforms and ladders with rails into deep water. The Kvarner gulf holds its heat, so it stays usable into early October.

places.name: The Korzo and Rijeka's Roman arch
places.note: Rijeka's promenade under Austro-Hungarian facades, with a Roman gate one street behind it and the market halls beyond. It is a working port, not a resort, and reads better on foot than its reputation.

places.name: Trsat castle and the 561 steps
places.note: A Frankopan keep on a bluff above the Rječina with a Greek nobleman's mausoleum in the garden and a pilgrimage church next door. The Petar Kružić stairway climbs to it from the city in 561 steps.

places.name: Museum of Modern and Contemporary Art, Rijeka
places.note: Rijeka's modern art museum in the restored Benčić industrial block, the best thing left over from the 2020 Capital of Culture year. Closed Mondays and almost empty on any other day.

places.name: Plavi podrum
places.note: A fish restaurant on the Volosko quay with a long Istrian and Slovenian wine list and a sommelier who will use it. Raw scampi, dentex, and a bill that matches the ambition.

places.name: Cake and coffee on the main street
places.note: The Habsburg ritual here is a hundred years old: a slice of cake in a high-ceilinged room off the main street. Sitting inside costs less than the terrace and the terrace is the point.

places.name: Vojak summit from Poklon
places.note: From the pass at 922m up to the stone tower on the 1,401m summit, ninety minutes each way through beech. Istria on one side, the Kvarner islands on the other, and cloud on top more often than anyone admits.

places.name: Vela Draga canyon
places.note: Free-standing limestone towers in a gorge below the Učka tunnel, seen from a short marked path off the old road. Climbers use the pillars; for everyone else it is a 40-minute stop, not a day.

places.name: Draga di Lovrana
places.note: A hillside restaurant above Lovran with one of the country's best cellars and game on the menu in autumn. You need the car, the booking and the appetite.

places.name: Vrbnik
places.note: A cliff-top town over the Vinodol channel with the žlahtina grape that grows nowhere else and a lane, Klančić, 43cm wide at its narrowest. The wine is light and cold and sold by the litre.

places.name: Baška and the Vela plaza
places.note: A 1.8km pebble beach at the island's south end under bare hills, with a path east to emptier coves. The bora funnels through here and can make the water unusable for a day at a time.

places.name: Krk town and the cathedral
places.note: A Roman-walled town with a basilica built over thermal baths and a Frankopan castle on the harbour. Twenty minutes off the bridge road and the best stop if you are only passing through.

places.name: The four campaniles of Rab
places.note: Four Romanesque bell towers in a line along one limestone spit, the tallest climbable for a few euro. The town's whole silhouette is those towers and you walk it end to end in half an hour.

places.name: Komrcar park
places.note: A pine park planted on bare karst in the 1880s by a forester who is buried in it, dropping to swimming ladders on the north shore. Five minutes from the old town and always cooler.

places.name: Paradise Beach at Lopar
places.note: One and a half kilometres of actual sand, shallow enough to wade fifty metres out, which is rare on this coast. Wall-to-wall families in July and August, empty and windy in May.

places.name: The Kalifront peninsula
places.note: Holm-oak forest and a string of bays on white tracks west of town, walkable or cyclable. Kandarola is where Edward VIII and Wallis Simpson swam naked in 1936 and it has been a naturist bay since.

places.name: The Rab crossbow tournament
places.note: A medieval crossbow contest revived in 1995 and shot with real bows at thirty paces, on 27 July and a handful of other dates. Outside those you get a smaller staged version for visitors.

places.name: A konoba in the old town
places.note: Stone-vaulted rooms in the lanes doing lamb, šurlice pasta and fish off the grill. Rab lamb is what to order here: the sheep graze salt-blown scrub and it tastes of it.

places.name: Rab cake
places.note: A spiral of almond and maraschino pastry sold in every second doorway, supposedly baked for Pope Alexander III in 1177. Buy the smallest one; it is very sweet and very rich.

places.name: Lubenice
places.note: A stone village of about a dozen residents on a 378m cliff over Sveti Ivan bay, with concerts in the ruined church in summer. The beach below is a 45-minute descent and a much longer climb back.

places.name: Beli and the griffon vultures
places.note: The centre at Beli tracks the Eurasian griffons nesting on the island's east cliffs, with marked trails from the village. The birds are resident year-round and easiest to see on morning thermals.

places.name: Valun and its Glagolitic tablet
places.note: A six-house fishing cove whose church porch holds an 11th-century stone inscribed in both Glagolitic and Latin, which is why linguists come. Parking is above the village and the walk down is steep.

places.name: St Donatus and the Roman forum
places.note: A 9th-century circular church standing directly on the paving and fallen columns of the Roman forum, stripped bare inside. The acoustics are the reason to go in, and the recitals are worth timing.

places.name: The Sea Organ
places.note: Marble steps with pipes underneath that the swell plays through holes in the promenade. It needs waves: on a flat calm evening it does almost nothing and people stand about waiting for a ferry wake.

places.name: The Greeting to the Sun
places.note: Nikola Bašić's circle of glass and photovoltaics set into the pavement, which lights up after dark on the day's own power. It works for about ten minutes after sunset and is packed for all of them.

places.name: Gold and Silver of Zadar
places.note: Reliquaries, gilded arms and painted panels kept by Benedictine nuns through two wars, shown in a couple of upstairs rooms. The best small collection in Dalmatia outside Split, and often empty.

places.name: Archaeological Museum Zadar
places.note: Liburnian, Roman and early Croatian material including the carved church furniture from Nin. The labelling is dry and the objects are first rank; an hour is enough.

places.name: Kalelarga and the sea walls
places.note: The Roman decumanus, still the street the whole town walks at 19:00, running from the land gate to the sea walls. The peninsula is fifteen minutes end to end, which is why two nights is enough.

places.name: Zadar green market and fish hall
places.note: One of the better markets on the coast, with the fish hall at the seaward end and cheese, pršut and figs inside the walls. It thins out badly after noon and shuts by early afternoon.

places.name: Nin and the salt pans
places.note: The 9th-century Holy Cross, called the smallest cathedral in the world, on a small walled island town with sandy shallows and mud baths beside it. Twenty minutes up the coast and a good half day.

places.name: The Ugljan ferry and Preko
places.note: A 25-minute car ferry to the island Zadar treats as its allotment, with olive terraces and a fort walk above Preko. This is what locals do with a free afternoon rather than a sight.

places.name: Pet bunara
places.note: On the square of the five wells, cooking Dalmatian food with some restraint and pouring a decent local list. One of the few kitchens on the peninsula not running a laminated tourist menu.

places.name: Maraschino on Narodni trg
places.note: The marasca cherry liqueur has been distilled here since 1821 and is drunk cold in small glasses. Ask for Maraska or the older Luxardo recipe rather than the sweet bottle sold to cruise passengers.

places.name: Gligora dairy at Kolan
places.note: Pag sheep's cheese from animals grazing salt-blown sage on bare rock, tasted as a flight at the dairy. The aged one is the reason this island appears on food maps at all.

places.name: Pag town and the salt pans
places.note: A 15th-century grid town laid out by Juraj Dalmatinac, with a lace museum and salt pans still working on the edge of it. The lace is genuinely handmade and the prices reflect the hours in it.

places.name: The Pag moonscape
places.note: The island's western side is stone stripped bare by the bora, with no soil and no trees for twenty kilometres. Drive it rather than walk it, and know that the bridge closes in the strongest wind.

places.name: Zrće beach
places.note: Four open-air clubs on a pebble spit outside Novalja, running from June to September. If you did not come for exactly that, it is a sunburnt car park with expensive drinks.

places.name: Velika Paklenica and Anića kuk
places.note: A gorge that narrows to a few metres under the 350m face of Anića kuk, the biggest climbing wall in this part of Europe. The walk to the Lugarnica hut and back is about four hours and mostly shaded.

places.name: The Paklenica tunnel
places.note: An unfinished Yugoslav command tunnel driven into the gorge wall, now an exhibition space held at about 12C. Ten minutes inside, and it explains the concrete you walked past at the entrance.

places.name: Vaganski vrh
places.note: At 1,757m the highest point of the Velebit, eight hours return with 1,400m of climb and no water on the route. A serious day that needs an early start and a settled forecast.

places.name: Kornat and the Opat cliffs
places.note: Eighty-nine islands of bare stone with no fresh water and almost no permanent residents. The crowns, the sheer seaward cliffs, are on the outer side; boats from Murter or Sali include the park fee and two swims.

places.name: Telašćica bay and Lake Mir
places.note: A long fjord-like bay on Dugi otok with 160m cliffs on its seaward side and a warm salt lake behind them. Most Kornati boats stop here and the walk up to the cliff top takes about thirty minutes.

places.name: Sali harbour
places.note: The village the southern Kornati boats leave from, with a few quayside kitchens cooking whatever came in. Quiet except in early August, when the fishermen's festival takes it over.

places.name: St James's Cathedral
places.note: Built entirely of interlocking stone with no timber or brick, finished in 1536, and ringed outside by 71 carved heads of ordinary Šibenik citizens. Juraj Dalmatinac's dome is why it is on the UNESCO list.

places.name: St Michael's Fortress
places.note: The hilltop fort above the cathedral, rebuilt in 2014 as an open-air stage with the channel and islands laid out below. The stair up through the old town is steep and completely unshaded.

places.name: Barone Fortress
places.note: A 1646 star fort on the hill behind town with an augmented-reality app and a wine terrace. Quieter than St Michael's, and the view inland towards the Krka is the better one.

places.name: St Nicholas Fortress
places.note: A 16th-century Venetian triangle built on an islet in the channel mouth, reachable only by boat from the Kanal. Visits are timed and cancelled in wind, so book it and check the forecast.

places.name: The Medieval Mediterranean Garden
places.note: A restored monastery cloister garden of box, lavender and herbs in four beds, with a cafe in the corner. Twenty minutes of shade in the middle of a stair town.

places.name: Šibenik market
places.note: A stepped market under the fortress with Skradin cherries in June and figs in August. This is a working town's market rather than a coastal display, and it is done by early afternoon.

places.name: Pelegrini
places.note: A Michelin-starred room on the cathedral steps with the best argument for Croatian wine anywhere in the country on its list. A real expense and the best meal on this coast.

places.name: A wine bar behind the cathedral
places.note: Dalmatian and Istrian bottles by the glass in the lanes: pošip, plavac, malvazija, and someone who can talk about them. Cheaper and more interesting than the waterfront terraces.

places.name: Diocletian's Palace and the substructures
places.note: A retirement palace with a town grown inside it, so the Roman streets are still addresses. The vaulted basement is where Game of Thrones filmed and where the souvenir stalls now are.

places.name: The cathedral of St Domnius and its campanile
places.note: Diocletian's mausoleum turned into a cathedral by the people he persecuted, with a bell tower of open stone stairs. The climb is exposed and not for anyone uneasy about heights.

places.name: Marjan hill
places.note: A pine hill straight off the west end of the Riva, with stairs to the Telegrin summit at 178m and swimming coves on the far side. Go before 09:00 in summer; there is little shade on the steps.

places.name: Pazar market and the Ribarnica
places.note: The open produce market east of the palace and the 1890 fish hall to the west, which famously has no flies because of the sulphur spring underneath it. Both are done by early afternoon.

places.name: Meštrović Gallery
places.note: Ivan Meštrović's own villa on the Marjan road holding his sculpture, with the Kaštelet chapel and its walnut reliefs a few hundred metres on. Closed Mondays and the best museum hour in Dalmatia.

places.name: Konoba Fetivi
places.note: A neighbourhood kitchen in Veli Varoš doing brodet and grilled fish with the football on in the corner. No tasting menu, no harbour view, and full of people who live here.

places.name: The Riva at 19:00
places.note: The whole town walks the waterfront before dinner and then sits over one coffee for an hour. It costs double what a back-street cafe charges and the hour itself is the point.

places.name: Zlatni rat
places.note: The shingle spit west of Bol that changes shape with the current and is on every poster of Croatia. It is pines, pebbles and paid loungers, and in August it is shoulder to shoulder.

places.name: Vidova gora
places.note: At 778m the highest point on any Adriatic island, with Zlatni rat and Hvar's ridge directly below. Two hours up from Bol on a marked path, or twenty minutes by car from Nerežišća.

places.name: Blaca hermitage
places.note: A monastery built into a cliff by monks fleeing the Ottomans in 1551, with its observatory and library left as they were. You walk the last twenty-five minutes in, or arrive by boat from Bol; hours are seasonal.

places.name: Pučišća and the stonemasons' school
places.note: A white harbour town where the secondary school still teaches hand stone-cutting and you can watch students work in term time. The stone from these quarries went into Diocletian's palace.

places.name: Murvica and the Dragon's Cave
places.note: An hour's climb above Murvica to a cave carved with a dragon, moons and angels by 15th-century Glagolitic monks. You must arrange the key-holder guide in advance and there is no shade on the path.

places.name: Konoba Kopačina
places.note: The island's lamb restaurant, roasted and grilled, in a village above Supetar since the early 1970s. They will tell you which slope the animal grazed, and it is not a marketing line.

places.name: Vis town: Kut and Luka
places.note: Two old quarters on either side of one bay, with Venetian captains' houses and a cricket ground left by the Napoleonic-era British garrison. The island was closed to foreigners until 1989, which is why it is not Hvar.

places.name: Komiža
places.note: A fishing town under Hum on the far side of the island, with a fishermen's museum in the Venetian tower and a reconstructed falkuša boat in it. The Blue Cave boats leave from this harbour.

places.name: The military tour: Tito's cave and the tunnels
places.note: Gun emplacements, a submarine pen, a rocket base and the cave Tito ran the Partisan war from in 1944, in a jeep because the tracks need one. The best half day on the island and only run with local guides.

places.name: Stiniva cove
places.note: A collapsed sea cave leaving a pebble beach behind a four-metre gap in the cliffs. The walk down is twenty steep minutes and the tour boats arrive around 11:00, so go early or go late.

places.name: Mount Hum
places.note: At 587m above Komiža, with the whole island and Biševo below and Italy on a very clear day. A rough road up or a two-hour climb, and the chapel of St Nicholas at the top is usually unlocked.

places.name: Pojoda
places.note: A walled courtyard in Kut doing fish, broad beans and the island's vugava white. It has been the reference restaurant on Vis for thirty years and needs booking in summer.

places.name: Vugava at a Vis cellar
places.note: Vugava is grown almost nowhere else, and the small producers here will pour it in a garage with a barrel in it. The cellars have no signs; ask whoever rented you the room.

places.name: The Blue Cave
places.note: Sunlight enters under the rock and lights the water from below, which needs late morning, flat sea and a small rowing boat through a 1.5m entrance. Twenty minutes inside, and cancelled outright in any swell.

places.name: Porat and Salbunara
places.note: Two sandy-ish bays on an island of about fifteen residents, with one konoba and no road worth the name. If your boat offers you an hour here, take it over a second cave.

places.name: Korčula old town
places.note: A fishbone street plan on a small peninsula, angled to catch the maestral and block the bora, which is the most intelligent medieval layout on this coast. You walk all of it in half an hour.

places.name: St Mark's Cathedral and treasury
places.note: A Gothic-Renaissance cathedral with a Tintoretto altarpiece and a climbable bell tower. The Marco Polo house nearby is an empty shell with a sign on it and is not worth its ticket.

places.name: The Moreška sword dance
places.note: A 16th-century sword dance performed with real blades by the town's own troupe, weekly in summer and on 29 July. Staged for visitors, and the dancers are local and take it entirely seriously.

places.name: Pupnatska Luka
places.note: The best cove on the island: a steep switchback down to pebbles, clear water and two beach bars. Parking is limited and full by 11:00 in July, so go early or go late.

places.name: Lumbarda and grk
places.note: The sandy end of the island, where grk, a white grape with no male flowers, grows in pure sand. The cellars pour it for a few euro and there are swimming bays either side of the road.

places.name: Konoba Mate
places.note: A family farm restaurant inland at Pupnat cooking what they grow, with žrnovski makaruni rolled by hand. You need a car or a taxi and it is worth both.

places.name: Massimo
places.note: A cocktail bar in the top of a 15th-century tower, reached by a vertical ladder, with drinks winched up on a pulley. The sunset is real and the queue starts well before 19:00.

places.name: Veliko and Malo jezero
places.note: Two connected saltwater lakes in a pine national park on the island's west end, ringed by a flat 9km path best done on a rented bicycle. The park ticket includes the launch to the islet.

places.name: St Mary's islet and monastery
places.note: A 12th-century Benedictine monastery on an island in a lake on an island, with a cafe in the cloister. The park boat runs out roughly hourly in season and hardly at all outside it.

places.name: The Odysseus cave
places.note: A collapsed sea cave near Babino Polje that you climb down into and swim out of into open water. It is a scramble with no ladder at the bottom, and the Calypso story is decoration.

places.name: Dingač and the Postup slopes
places.note: Plavac mali on 45-degree limestone above the sea, with a one-lane tunnel through the ridge from Potomje to the vines. Cellars in Potomje and Trstenik pour the real Dingač at a fraction of restaurant prices.

places.name: The Ston walls
places.note: Five and a half kilometres of 14th-century Republic wall over the hill between Ston and Mali Ston, built to guard the salt pans that paid for Dubrovnik. A real climb with no shade, so do it early.

places.name: The Mali Ston oyster beds
places.note: European flat oysters grown in the Mali Ston channel and eaten at quayside tables with lemon and bread. The season peaks in spring and the mussels here are as good as the oysters.

places.name: The city walls circuit
places.note: Two kilometres round the top of the walls, one direction only, at about 35 euro in season. Be at the Pile steps for 08:00 or go after 17:00: from 10:00 to 16:00 in July it is a queue in full sun.

places.name: The Stradun and the Onofrio fountains
places.note: One limestone street polished by four centuries of feet, rebuilt to a single plan after the 1667 earthquake. At 07:00 it belongs to the cats and the bakers; by 11:00 to three cruise ships.

places.name: The Rector's Palace
places.note: The Republic's seat of government, where the elected rector served one month and was not allowed to leave the building. The rooms and the cells are the story rather than the paintings on the walls.

places.name: The Franciscan monastery and pharmacy
places.note: A Romanesque cloister of paired columns and a pharmacy that has been dispensing since 1317, one of the oldest in Europe. The quietest place inside the walls in the middle of the day.

places.name: Mount Srđ and the Homeland War museum
places.note: Four hundred metres straight above the old town by cable car or an hour of zig-zags, with a Napoleonic fort holding an unsentimental exhibition on the 1991 to 1995 siege. Walk it at dawn, not at noon.

places.name: War Photo Limited
places.note: Two floors of conflict photography with a permanent room on the Yugoslav wars, curated by a photographer who covered them. The most serious thing inside the walls, and it closes for the winter.

places.name: Lokrum
places.note: A wooded island fifteen minutes offshore with a Benedictine ruin, a botanical garden, loose peacocks and a small salt lake to swim in. The last boat back is earlier than people assume.

places.name: Gruž market
places.note: The working market by the ferry port where the city actually shops, fish hall included. Twenty minutes' walk or a short bus from the walls, and nothing in it is priced for visitors.

places.name: Restaurant Kopun
places.note: On the square by the Jesuit church, cooking capon in the medieval honey and lemon recipe the town revived. Inside the walls and priced better than anything on the Stradun.

places.name: Buža
places.note: A bar on the rocks outside the south wall, reached through a hole in it, where people jump off the cliff into deep water. Cash only, dear, and worth exactly one round for the position.

places.name: Lopud and Šunj beach
places.note: A car-free island an hour from Gruž with a Franciscan fortress-monastery, a garden villa and real sand at Šunj, twenty minutes' walk over the hill. The ferry timetable decides the shape of the day.

places.name: Šipan
places.note: The largest and least visited of the islands, with Dubrovnik nobles' summer villas at both harbours and an olive-terraced road between them. Two konobas, no crowd, and not much shade.

places.name: Tvrđa
places.note: A complete 18th-century Habsburg baroque fortress quarter on the Drava, built after the Ottomans left and now half university and half bars. It is the reason to come to Osijek and it takes a morning.

places.name: Museum of Slavonia
places.note: Slavonia's collection in the old Tvrđa guardhouse, strongest on Roman Mursa and on the Ottoman-to-Habsburg turnover. Closed Mondays, quiet on every other day, and patchy in English.

places.name: The pedestrian suspension bridge
places.note: A 1980 footbridge over the Drava to the flood-plain side, where the city walks, runs and cycles. Flat, green, and the best evening hour in town.

places.name: The Kompa ferry
places.note: A small cable ferry that has crossed to the Osijek beach since long before the bridge, still running in summer for a euro or two. Two minutes each way and entirely a local ritual.

places.name: The Europska avenija villas
places.note: A boulevard of 1900s secession villas between the centre and Tvrđa, tiled and stuccoed and mostly unrestored. Ten minutes of looking up that almost no visitor does.

places.name: Osijek market and kulen
places.note: The central market for kulen, the paprika-heavy pork sausage, plus paprika paste and river fish. Buy kulen from a stall with one label and a queue in front of it.

places.name: Fiš paprikaš by the Drava
places.note: Carp and catfish stewed with a hard hand of paprika and served with home-made noodles. The dish of this river, and the good versions are outside the centre rather than on the main square.

places.name: Kopački rit by boat
places.note: One of Europe's largest inland floodplains, where the Drava meets the Danube, seen from a flat boat with white-tailed eagles and black storks overhead. Spring flood and autumn migration are the point; July is mosquitoes.

places.name: Kormoran
places.note: Game and river fish at the park edge: wild boar, carp on a board, and a cellar of Baranja wine. The only serious kitchen out here and it fills with Hungarian day trippers.

places.name: Vukovar water tower
places.note: The shelled water tower left exactly as 1991 left it, now with a lift to a viewing deck, an hour southeast of Osijek. A hard, plain memorial, and the town around it is still visibly rebuilding.
